title: Forest for the Trees

beats.what: A voice on the radio recites a nursery rhyme; it cuts out before anyone can respond
Jim and Randall argue about the radio voice and whether residents are being watched by orchestrators of an experiment
Elgin woke up drowning in real water after a bathtub nightmare; Jade reports a bug burn from a dream
Jade confronts Victor at the diner about the symbol on the tunnel walls; Victor refuses and tries to leave
Jade aggressively corners Victor at the Matthews house demanding tunnel information
Victor gives Julie his old coat and a portrait drawing; warns her to keep pictures for remembering
Jim sends Ethan and Victor away, then goes to stay the night in the RV with Randall to watch the creatures unobserved
Jade and Randall interview Sara about her brother Nathan; Randall presses her on whether Nathan is really dead
Julie visits Colony House; Victor reveals his hidden pictures were stored so no one else would die
Cicadas swarm out of the dissected creature in the clinic basement; the body is not as inert as assumed
Victor's hidden trunk contains childhood drawings; one shows Eloise running toward a tower structure
Eloise's fate revealed: Victor saw her go toward the tower but she never made it inside the tree

character_beats.beat: Wants to protect the people he cares about by suppressing knowledge; gives Julie his coat and portrait while simultaneously hiding the tunnel drawings that could save everyone
Wants proof that human orchestrators are behind the town; drags Randall into a dangerous overnight watch, filtering every piece of evidence through a conspiracy frame
Wants answers enough to weaponise his aggression against Victor, a child; after the confrontation he shifts to careful observation as strategy

key_lines.line: I put them somewhere so I would never have to remember.
key_lines.why: Victor explains the hidden drawings: his amnesia is self-imposed, not the place's doing

key_lines.line: So that no one else would die.
key_lines.why: Completes the above: Victor believes his knowledge is a kill switch that ends lives
Victor's three-word verdict on people who look for answers; applies to his own mother
Victor refuses to desire escape; the place is not a trap to him, it is his entire world

open_loops: What are the drawings Victor hid and what do they show about the night everyone died?
Does Victor know a specific path to the tower, or only the bottle tree route?
Why are the cicadas still active inside the supposedly dead creature?
Is Nathan actually alive or was Sara's fraticide real?
What does the nursery rhyme voice on the radio want from the residents?

payoffs.what: The creature's body releases cicadas that match Jade's dream bugs; dreams are now confirmed as physically consequential

payoffs.plants_from: earlier episodes (Victor's guarded silence about the tunnels)
payoffs.what: Julie discovers Victor hid an entire trunk of childhood drawings specifically to prevent deaths

contradiction.wants: to protect the people he loves from death by withholding dangerous knowledge
contradiction.does: hands Julie a portrait drawing he says is for remembering in case something happens to him, simultaneously inviting the grief he claims to be preventing

tone_notes: The episode opens with two long silences back to back: 49.9 seconds (02:59-03:49) then 129.6 seconds (03:51-06:01). The second is the longest single silence in this five-episode run and places the post-radio-nursery-rhyme shock in near-total quiet. Minutes 6-16 run dense (126-162 w/min) through the experimental-theory argument, then drop sharply to 14 w/min at minute 32 when Victor sees the trunk. The lowest density minutes bracket the episode's most emotionally loaded scene.
